# Purpose

This folder documents a **gentle, metadata-only** scrape of [FishWise Professional](https://www.fishwisepro.com) to collect **image attributions** (species, photographer, filenames, URLs) for Chaetodontidae. No images are downloaded; we only record who to credit and where the images live. The scrape uses the existing FishWise species ID (SID) cache and one HTTP request per species.

# Data source

- **Site:** FishWise Professional (`fishwisepro.com`) — ASP.NET + DevExpress, AJAX-heavy.
- **Scope:** Chaetodontidae (130 species in our project list).
- **Pages used:** Per-species image galleries:  
  `https://www.fishwisepro.com/Pictures/?SID={sid}&Find=0`  
  The `sid` values come from `data/fishwise/fishwise_sid_cache.json`, which was populated by:

  1. Paginating the family gallery (fid=438) with Selenium and reading SIDs from image filenames.
  2. For species not seen in the gallery, resolving SIDs via the site’s **Quick Search** form and parsing result links.

  See `scripts/download/update_fishwise_sid_cache.py` and the main project notes for SID discovery details.

# Scraping strategy

## Query design

- **One request per species.** We do not re-scrape the family gallery; we use the cached SIDs and hit the per-species gallery URL for each of the 130 target species.
- **Single page per species.** Each `/Pictures/?SID={sid}&Find=0` response is one HTML page. We parse it once; we do not paginate within a species (if a species had many images and multiple pages, only the first page is scraped — acceptable for attribution inventory).
- **No images downloaded.** We only parse the HTML to extract metadata; no image bytes are requested or saved.

## Parsing

From each gallery page we extract `<img>` tags that match:

- `src="/pics/{JPG|GIF}/TN/TN{filename}"`  
  Filename format: `{6-digit SID}F...W....{ext}` (e.g. `045446F000024W000001.jpg`).
- `alt="Species - Photographer"`  
  We split on the last `" - "` to get species name and photographer (attribution).

We record: `species`, `photographer`, `filename`, `thumb_url`, `full_url`, `format`, `sid`.

## Politeness

- **Delay between requests:** Default 2.5 s (configurable via `--delay`). No parallel requests.
- **User-Agent:** Identifies the script as a metadata scrape (`Chaetodontidae-attribution-scrape`).
- **Timeout:** 30 s per request; on failure we log and continue.
- **No retries** in the default script to avoid bursts; re-run the script to retry failed species.

## Output

- **File:** `attributions.csv` in this folder.
- **Columns:** `species`, `photographer`, `filename`, `thumb_url`, `full_url`, `format`, `sid`.

# How to run

From the project root or from this folder:

```bash
cd /path/to/downloading-fish-images-2026/fishwise_attributions
python scrape_attributions.py --delay 2.5
```

Optional:

- `--dry-run` — print URLs only, no HTTP requests.
- `--delay 3` — increase delay between requests.

# Summary of scraped attributions

After running the scraper, the chunk below summarizes the attribution data (run Quarto render with the CSV present).

```{r attributions-summary}
attrib_file <- "attributions.csv"
if (file.exists(attrib_file)) {
  attr <- read.csv(attrib_file)
  cat("**Total image records:**", nrow(attr), "\n\n")
  cat("**Species with at least one image:**", length(unique(attr$species)), "\n\n")
  cat("**Unique photographers (top 15):**\n\n")
  photog <- as.data.frame(sort(table(attr$photographer), decreasing = TRUE))
  names(photog) <- c("Photographer", "Count")
  knitr::kable(head(photog, 15))
} else {
  cat("No `attributions.csv` found. Run `python scrape_attributions.py` first.\n")
}
```
